title: Veridian Therapeutics outbound + pilot sketch
body:
Context / why Veridian?
- Mid-size biotech (Veridian Therapeutics). Focus: clinical trial document ingestion, automated protocol summarization, and role-specific assistant for clinical ops.
- Regulatory sensitivity: PHI adjacent (trial IDs, participant notes). They mentioned wanting VPC/private deployment and KMS.
- Heard via intro (Dr. R. Mendez, ex-Redwood advisor). They’re exploring LLMs for automation but are worried about hallucinations and auditability.
- Opportunity: quick pilot (6–8 weeks) to show cost/latency gains vs their current CPU-bound LLM endpoints + show traceable evals and prompt-set monitoring.

Key stakeholders (mapped from discovery notes)
- Dr. Rosa Mendez (advisor / internal champion) – clinical ops, cares about accuracy and audit trails.
- Jordan Kim – Head of Data Platform (primary technical owner). Wants VPC + HSM + predictable latency for nightly batch runs.
- Elaine Park – Director, Regulatory Affairs (security/compliance sign-off).
- Tony Alvarez – ML Eng manager (day-to-day integration).

ICP pain points / explicit asks heard so far
- Current system: slow, high per-token cost for nightly transcript embeddings; times out on long docs.
- Need: private deployment option (VPC/on-prem), clear KMS integration, and ability to pin model versions for audits.
- Must be able to trace prompts -> outputs for regulatory review.
- Prefer a gradual roll: pilot on non-PHI subset of documents, then broaden.

Pilot hypothesis (what success looks like)
- Technical: 50% reduction in per-token inference cost for nightly batch embedding pipeline; 2x throughput on longest docs (50k tokens) without a significant latency SLA breach for interactive QA.
- QC: end-to-end traceability in Console with evals for 3 canonical prompt sets; no increase in hallucination rate vs baseline (<= 3 regressions detected).
- Business: internal champion secures buy-in for a 12-month Dedicated contract if pilot passes (cost model + SLOs favorable).

Pilot scope (MVP)
- Scope: 1) nightly batch ingestion + embeddings for trial documents (subset: protocol summaries, consent forms) 2) API-driven interactive QA for clinical ops (bounded prompt templates).
- Mode: Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with private control plane depending on legal. Start with VPC private control plane if possible.
- Deliverables: deployment runbook, Console eval dashboards, canary rollback plan, short training session for Tony's team.

Technical notes / integration constraints (notes for infra convo)
- KMS: They want HSM-backed keys (Yubi or cloud HSM). Need to confirm supported providers (AWS CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM).
- Network: strict egress rules; no outbound to public internet from processing hosts. Need guide for VPN/IP allowlist.
- Data residency: US-only (secondary EU region for global docs).
- Models: recommend starting with a quantized open model + Redwood-verified profile for cost; fallback to larger model for eval/regressions.
- Prefix caching: huge win for repeated template prompts in their QA flows. Highlight auto-prefix/KV caching.

Outreach sequence (suggested)
1) Email 0 (intro via Rosa) – short, reference intro, ask for 30m to align pilot goals. (see draft below)
2) Follow-up 3 days – one-pager + sample pilot timeline + cost ballpark for 8-week pilot.
3) Technical sync w/ Jordan & Tony (30–45m) – bring infra + security checklist.
4) Regulatory touchpoint w/ Elaine – share audit/traceability artifacts; propose white-glove onboarding for compliance review.
5) Internal proposal (we prepare deck + SoW) – send to them 3–4 working days after positive technical sync.

Email draft: intro (to send from Rosa or Claire)
Subject: Intro from Dr. Mendez — quick chat on a secure LLM pilot for Veridian
Hi Jordan / Elaine / Tony,

Dr. Rosa Mendez suggested I reach out — she mentioned you’re evaluating LLMs for clinical ops automation and want a private, auditable setup. I’m Claire on the Redwood Partnerships team. We help regulated teams run inference with VPC/on‑prem options, HSM integrations, and built-in audit + eval tooling.

Quick ask: 30 minutes to align on the pilot scope and blockers. We can show a short runbook and a cost/throughput outline tailored to your nightly batch workloads.

If helpful, I can include Tony and Jordan on a single sync and invite one of our infra engineers. Proposed times: Tue/Wed next week 10–12 or Thurs 2–4 PT.

Thanks — Claire

Cold-leaning alternative (if intro not available)
Subject: Reducing inference cost for trial documents (pilot idea)
Hi Jordan — I’m Claire (Redwood Inference). Quick idea: run an 8-week pilot to cut per-token cost for your nightly embeddings and add traceability for audit. No infra changes up front; we can run on a VPC/private control plane. 30 min to show sample outputs?

Objection handling cheat-sheet
- "We can’t expose data to external vendors": clarify Private/VPC and private control plane option + SOC2/ISO artifacts + ephemeral nodes + audit logs. Offer white-glove legal/infosec runbook.
- "We already built something in-house": emphasize build vs buy math (TCO calc), operational burden of batching/KV cache, and time-to-value; offer a quick A/B on last N days of throughput to quantify difference.
- "Hallucinations are unacceptable": propose eval plan with baseline prompt set, automatic regression alerts, and human-in-loop gating for high-risk outputs. Show prior case study numbers (anonymized).
- "Pricing/commits are risky": offer a short reserved capacity pilot or trial credits + opt-in to a reserved commit only if SLOs met.

Metrics / proposal skeleton for the SoW
- Baseline metrics to capture before pilot: current tokens/day, avg seq length, batch window duration, current 95th latency for interactive QA, current cost per 1M tokens.
- Pilot commitments: 8 weeks, Redwood provides infra/config + 2 infra eng hours/wk + 1 PM touchpoint/wk + 2 training sessions.
- Acceptance criteria: cost reduction >= 30% OR throughput improvement >= 2x AND no QA regression beyond agreed thresholds.

Risks / unknowns to validate early
- Legal's allowance for Private vs Dedicated (they may insist on certain providers).
- Willingness to share sample doc types (non-PHI) for eval.
- KMS/HSM compatibility with their vendor.

Next immediate steps (what I want to do this week)
- Send intro draft to Rosa for a warm intro. (ACTION: Claire)
- Build quick cost/back-of-envelope for their nightly pipeline using a 10k/seq assumption and 1.2M tokens/day. (ACTION: Marcus)
- Pull prior healthcare case study (redacted) and short deck for Elaine. (ACTION: Priya)
- Prepare infra checklist for Jordan + Tony and highlight VPC onboarding timeline (ACTION: Tony to review with infra).

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Could pitch Redwood Optimize to automate batching suggestions — big ROI with long docs.
- Consider offering a pre-pilot hosted run (no production data) to show delta quickly if they’re nervous about early private onboarding.
- If Legal pushes back on HSM, propose a staged KMS approach: cloud-managed HSM -> customer HSM -> on-prem HSM.

Open questions to resolve on next call
- Which KMS vendors acceptable? Any procurement constraints?
- Do they require data residency beyond US (specific states)?
- Who will own the acceptance tests? (Tony/clinical ops?)
- Are there embargo/blackout windows for trial doc processing?
notes_summary: Scratchpad for outbound motion to Veridian Therapeutics: pilot hypothesis, stakeholders, outreach sequence, technical constraints, objection handling, metrics and next steps.
